data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's answer assumes the non-expert panel's reliability advantage comes from faithful execution of the checklist author's 'frozen-good-theory,' explicitly arguing the value is not aggregation/Condorcet. But the problem asks whether a panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist will, on average, be more reliable than a single expert. SRC_002 gives no argument or evidence that panel aggregation is not the operative reliability mechanism: Condorcet-style error reduction and redundancy could yield higher reliability than a single expert even if the checklist is only a surface proxy with no superior causal structure. By attributing reliability solely to checklist-theory quality, SRC_002 fails to argue the actual comparative claim (panel-vs-single) posed by the problem.
